title: WSLProxy API Gateway policy (api_gw)
description: The `api_gw` block on a server JSON (data/servers/<env>/host:<hostname>.json), or on a rule as an override. Every field is optional except `enabled`; a server without an api_gw block behaves exactly as before. Policy changes take effect on the next request — no nginx reload.

enabled.description: Master switch. false (or absent) disables the whole package for this server — this is also the rollback lever.

tenant_id.description: Isolation key for every shared-dict counter. Defaults to "<profile_id>/<server_name>", so each server in each environment gets its own quotas. Set it explicitly only to make several hostnames deliberately share one quota.

modules.description: Which modules run. Absent means all of them. A comma-separated string is also accepted, for admin UIs that flatten arrays.

real_ip.description: Trusted-proxy handling. With no trusted_cidrs the forwarded header is never consulted and the TCP peer is the client — the only safe default.

trusted_cidrs.description: IPv4 CIDRs whose forwarded headers are believed. Anything outside this set has its header ignored entirely.

recursive.description: true walks the header right-to-left past trusted hops to the first untrusted address. false takes the last entry, which is correct when exactly one trusted proxy sits in front.

echo_downstream.description: Also return the id to the caller.

accept_inbound.description: false always mints a fresh id and ignores what the client sent.

allow.description: Media types without parameters. "application/*" and "*/*" wildcards are supported.

exempt_paths.description: Segment-aware path prefixes, or "~<regex>". Uploads and form-encoded webhooks belong here.

max_body_bytes.description: 0 disables the api_gw check; nginx client_max_body_size remains the hard backstop. Enforced from Content-Length, so a chunked request with no declared length is not caught here.

require_content_length.description: Reject a body-bearing method with no Content-Length (411). Closes the chunked-upload hole in max_body_bytes at the cost of breaking streaming clients.

token_typ.description: Advisory check on the `typ` field of a JWS header. Never an authorisation decision — the signature is not verified here.

origins.description: Exact origins, "*", or a single-label wildcard such as "https://*.example.com". An empty list allows nothing.

credentials.description: With credentials on, a "*" origin echoes the concrete origin instead, because browsers reject the literal wildcard with credentials.

preflight_continue.description: true forwards the OPTIONS upstream after attaching the headers.

ivt.description: Invalid-traffic guard. Signals are weighted and summed; the request is rejected only when the total reaches block_threshold and the mode is "block".

mode.description: audit = evaluate silently; monitor = also emit X-WSL-IVT; block = reject at the threshold.

allow.description: When non-empty, anything outside the list scores method_denied.

path_denylist.description: PCRE patterns matched case-insensitively against the URI.

require_auth_shape.description: Score a malformed Authorization header ("<scheme> <token>" is the only accepted shape). An absent header is not malformed.

strip_header_prefixes.description: Headers starting with any of these are removed from the upstream request in every non-disabled mode, and score header_spoof. Use for internal headers the origin trusts.

enabled.description: Defaults to true when max_requests is set.

auth.description: Optional edge authentication. The default keeps the origin authoritative.

strategy.description: passthrough forwards the credential untouched; none marks the scope public; jwt and api_key enforce at the edge.

public_paths.description: Segment-aware prefixes (or "~<regex>") that skip every strategy. "/health" covers "/health/live" but not "/healthz-other".

protected_paths.description: When non-empty, the strategy applies only inside these prefixes; everything else stays passthrough.

allow_unverified_subject.description: Let a passthrough route read an unverified `sub` claim so rate profiles can key on it. It is a fairness key, never an authorisation decision; set false to fall back to the client IP.

secret.description: Inline key. Prefer secret_ref — never commit a real value.

secret_ref.description: "secret://<record-id>#<key>" or "env://VAR_NAME". An unresolvable ref rejects the request; it never resolves to the ref string.

cookie.description: Cookie name to fall back to when the header is absent.

leeway.description: Clock-skew tolerance in seconds for exp and nbf.

claim_key.description: Which claim becomes the consumer id.

query_param.description: Optional fallback location. Query strings land in access logs — prefer the header.

keys_ref.description: A single ref resolving to a comma- or whitespace-separated key bundle.

default_profile.description: Applied to any request whose route names no profile. An unknown name is created as unlimited rather than blocking traffic.

profiles.description: Named quotas. The built-ins health, auth, public, standard, expensive and webhook are present unless overridden; tenants may add their own.

key.description: What the quota is counted against. consumer and jwt.sub fall back to the client IP when no subject was resolved — never to one shared bucket.

algorithm.description: Overrides the module default for this profile.

audit.description: One structured JSON line per request on the nginx error log. Credentials are never included: the redaction set below is ADDED to a baseline (authorization, proxy-authorization, cookie, set-cookie, x-api-key, api-key, x-auth-token) that cannot be removed.

tag.description: Leading token on the log line, for the shipper's parser.

sample_rate.description: Rejections and 4xx/5xx are always kept regardless of the rate.

include_query.description: Off by default: query strings routinely carry tokens. Truncated to 512 chars when on.

include_client_ip.description: Off by default; client_key_hash (tenant-salted) is always present.

include_headers.description: Extra headers to capture, truncated to 256 chars. Anything in the redaction set is dropped even if named here.

redact_headers.description: Additional header names to drop. Added to the baseline, never replacing it.

routes.description: The route policy matrix. The most specific match wins: `equals` beats `starts_with`, a longer prefix beats a shorter one, regex sits below both, and ties break on declaration order. Selection is deterministic and independent of the order routes appear in.

name.description: Route class label. Appears in the audit line.

methods.description: Scope the route to these methods. Absent matches any.

cors.description: Per-route CORS overrides, merged over the server policy.
